substeps.caption: After a run: below 400 C the operator turns off Melting Pressure and Pressure Control and presses Vent Valve (DAL SOP, Cooldown 2-3). The furnace's lid is held by a draw latch and a pneumatic bolt.

At atmosphere the bolt goes back: it locks the lever whenever the furnace is pumped or pressurised (Kalicki, AMAZEMET, install call 22:04). Its release on venting is our reading of that, not seen in a video.
Arm 1 takes the lever near its free end, the 2F-85's pads on its two side flanges, 133 mm below the pivot. The lever pivots at its top and hangs flat over its base (T4 5:35.5).

Out and up about the top pivot. The loop's pivot first draws away from the hook: the seal is squeezed 0.60 mm more at dead centre, 18 deg out; the pull peaks just before it, about 100 N (estimate; 200 N if stiff), and is zero there. Past 41 deg the loop is slack.

Arm 1 lets the lever back to 42 deg, where it rests on the slack loop, whose bar sits on the keeper's hook again; then it lets go. The lid is still hooked on: the loop has to come off the keeper first.

Unlatching: arm 1 takes the loop by its two legs, from outside, clear of the lever and the keeper. Lifting it raises the lever on the loop's pin, and the bar rides up the keeper's plate, over the hook's lip.

Clear of the lip, it tips the loop out just past upright and lets the lever down on the loop's pin, flat onto its base.

Then it opens its fingers and lets the loop fall: it tips out over the lever and hangs down over it (T4 5:08; T4 5:29.5-5:35 read backwards: the hand lifts the bar off the lip and lets the loop fall, while a second hand holds the lever up; one-handed, the lever goes down first).

Down through dead centre (18 deg): the loop goes taut, the seal takes 0.60 mm more squeeze, the pull peaks at about 100 N; past it the loop pulls the lever shut onto its base. Over centre, it stays shut.

Vacuum Pump and Vacuum Valve (Cold purge 7): as the pressure changes the bolt comes in and locks the lever. The check the machine allows: the furnace reaches about -850 mbar and holds, with no hiss.

If it can't reach -0.85 bar or the lid hisses (DAL SOP troubleshooting): vent, open the latch, shorten the loop half a turn at its lock nuts (an adjuster we assume: the model and the footage show none), close it and pump again.

Margins (chapter 2's stability(), 131 kg plates): MiR 1 would tip at 783 N and slide at 952 N on the lever (it needs 100-200); MiR 2, with the lid's 58 N on its knob, would tip at 1546 N. No arm presses on the lid.
